description_full: Ardmore Shipping Corporation engages in the seaborne transportation of petroleum products and chemicals worldwide. The company's fleet consists of 26 vessels, including 25 owned Eco-design vessels and one chartered-in vessels. It serves oil majors, national oil companies, oil and chemical traders, chemical companies, and pooling service providers. The company was founded in 2010 and is headquartered in Hamilton, Bermuda.

Each employee generates $1.4M of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $49K per employee reflects an ownership culture.
financial_summary: Ardmore Shipping Corporation is a small-cap industrials business with a $797M market cap on $310M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -11% over the past three years and +7% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 22% against a 8% cost of capital — a 14-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $81M in free cash flow — roughly 26 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.99× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.6× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 7.8×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.5%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 9.8% of the shares.
